title: Shortest Path in Binary Matrix
statement: In an n by n binary grid, 0 is open and 1 is blocked. Return the length of the shortest clear path from (0, 0) to (n - 1, n - 1). You may move to any of the eight neighbors. Return -1 if the path does not exist. A path length counts cells, including both ends.
hints: Unweighted grid movement is BFS, not Dijkstra.
If either corner is blocked, return -1 before searching. Mark cells visited when you enqueue them.

approaches.name: DFS
approaches.explanation: DFS does not give the shortest path in an unweighted graph unless you explore every walk.

approaches.name: BFS
approaches.explanation: The first time you reach the corner is optimal.

editorial: BFS layers are distances in an unweighted graph. Start at the top-left with distance 1 if it is open. Expand all eight neighbors that are open and unvisited. The distance stored when you first reach the bottom-right is the answer.
